markers.name: Monument Area
markers.desc: The heart of the village. Anchored by our All-Ireland Victory Centennial monument, marking the 1900 hurling final.

markers.name: The Old Forge
markers.desc: Restored forge beside Corcoran's Bar parking. Heritage feature on the main street.

markers.name: Blackcastle (Norman Castle)
markers.desc: Historic Norman castle remains on the western approach to the village.

markers.name: Liathmore Monastic Site
markers.desc: Sixth-century monastic site 2.8km east of the village, founded by the saint who gave our school its name.

markers.name: Bannon's Bar Lounge
markers.desc: Pub on the main street (L4202).

markers.name: Tully's Nearby
markers.desc: Pub and shop on the main street.

markers.name: Corcoran's Bar & Shop
markers.desc: Bar with separate shop entrance on the right-hand side.

markers.name: Sensory Garden
markers.desc: Beside the school. Timber pergola, drystone amphitheatre, gravel paths and living willow features.

markers.name: St James Church & Grounds
markers.desc: St James Church on the main street, the calm centrepiece of the village.

markers.name: Two-Mile-Borris Cemetery
markers.desc: The village cemetery on the western edge, with original gates and a 2025 extension.

markers.name: New Cemetery Entrance
markers.desc: New entrance to the enlarged cemetery on the L4202.

markers.name: Old Road Triangle (N75 Diversion)
markers.desc: Wedge of mature trees stranded between the old and new N75 alignments after the 2010 reroute. A no-touch wildlife refuge inside the village edge.

markers.name: Scoil Mochaomhóg Naofa NS
markers.desc: Our village national school, on the L4202 since 1846. Active Green Schools programme.

markers.name: Castle Park
markers.desc: Housing estate north of the main street.

markers.name: Ned Hayes Park
markers.desc: Develop bedding in green strips, add climbers on boundary walls (adjudicator recommendation).

markers.name: Glen Carraig
markers.desc: Eastern estate. Develop wildflower garden at extensive entrance green area (adjudicator recommendation).

markers.name: Cluain Na Seimre
markers.desc: Northern estate off the Ballyduff Road.

markers.name: Fanning Park
markers.desc: Estate south of the main street, near the cemetery. The entrance corner is a candidate for the village biodiversity corridor with a mature flowering Hawthorn already in place.

markers.name: Dún Na Rí
markers.desc: Western estate.

markers.name: Ardleigh
markers.desc: Estate off the L4202 east of the village centre.

markers.name: Leighton Manor Estate
markers.desc: Eastern estate.

markers.name: Meadow Brook
markers.desc: Estate south of the main street.

markers.name: Two-Mile-Borris Transport Museum
markers.desc: Car and transport museum (temporarily closed).

markers.name: Dempsey & Harold Motors site (redevelopment)
markers.desc: Former Dempsey & Harold Motors garage, being redeveloped by Roadvacs (Irl) Limited as their Tipperary base.

markers.name: Approach: West (Thurles)
markers.desc: Western approach via the N75 from Thurles direction. Spring 2026 Dutch Master daffodil planting along this stretch. (The L4202 is the road inside the village itself.)

markers.name: Approach: East (Horse & Jockey)
markers.desc: Eastern approach on the L4202 from Horse & Jockey direction.

markers.name: Approach: North (Ballyduff)
markers.desc: Northern approach via Ballyduff Road.

markers.name: Approach: South (N75)
markers.desc: Southern approach via the N75 from the M8 motorway (Junction 5) direction. Same road as the western approach. The N75 links Thurles in the north-west to the M8 in the south.

markers.name: Village Seating Area
markers.desc: Bench seating area on the western end of the village with box topiary planters, gravel path, and pollinator-friendly wildflower planting.

markers.name: Black River Crossing
markers.desc: The Black River (tributary of the River Drish) flows alongside Blackcastle and under the road. Wildlife includes coots and ducks.

bogWalk.name: Bog Walk Loop
bogWalk.description: A looped walk through bogland starting from the Clover entrance, heading north through open bog, and returning via Clover Lane off the Ballyduff Road.
